attacks.claim: Dark mode breaks: .day-card hardcodes background #ffffff while text color uses var(--text), which becomes near-white (#f2f2f7) in dark mode. Tile titles (h3/h2) inherit light text on a white card, making them unreadable for the ~30% of users in dark mode. .meta uses --muted (#a1a1a6) on white, which is also low contrast.

QA covered only light mode (Chrome 1440 light, Safari iPhone 14 light). Dark mode was never tested despite being supported since v5 and used by ~30% of users. The Lighthouse accessibility 100 score was evidently not run in dark mode, so it does not catch the contrast bug.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass

attacks.claim: The most frequent planner action (add recipe ingredients to the shopping list, 9.4 times/week per WAU, 64% on mobile) is moved from a one-tap button to a 5-step flow (tile, recipe page, Ingredients tab, servings sheet, Add to list). This contradicts the brief's own usage data and will likely hurt the core metric. The bulk 'Generate shopping list' action does not replace per-recipe adds.
attacks.evidence: The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles. ... tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list"

attacks.claim: Adding a recipe to the shopping list was one tap and now takes about five taps with page navigations, repeated roughly 9 times a week per user, mostly on mobile. Rolling out to 100% with no staged exposure or experiment makes the friction impossible to measure before it hits everyone.

The fixed 72px bottom action bar on mobile has no bottom padding on .planner, and Sunday is the last child of .planner. The bar will cover the last day card's content and its buttons. There is no safe-area-inset handling for iPhone home indicators.
attacks.evidence: Sunday is the last child of .planner; .action-bar { position: fixed; ... bottom: 0; height: 72px }; .planner padding: 16px

attacks.claim: Tile images have empty alt text. That is acceptable if decorative, but the 'Swap' buttons are not named per recipe, so screen-reader users hear repeated identical 'Swap' labels. The <nav> action bar has no aria-label and holds actions, not navigation.

Rollback is described as flipping the flag, but the rollout has no stated thresholds for the watch metrics (bounce, additions/WAU) and no staged ramp. Regressions would be detected only after 100% exposure.
attacks.evidence: Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.
